title: Emotional
coreMove: Make the consequence matter by tying it to one human stake, identity, dignity, or meaningful cost.
sourcePressure: The source treats emotion as making people care through one person, identity, dignity, self-interest, and meaning, with Floyd Lees Iraq dining example grounding morale and dignity.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Equating emotion with sadness, hype, guilt, or inspirational language.

sourceAnchors.name: one-person-versus-many framing
sourceAnchors.detail: the sidecar says one-person-versus-many framing supports the idea that abstract scale often fails to move feeling
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: One person can make the stake visible when the crowd has become too large to feel.

sourceAnchors.name: analytical framing
sourceAnchors.detail: the sidecar says analytical framing can reduce giving or emotional response compared with a humanized case
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Analysis can cool the very concern a message needs, especially when the person has disappeared into the numbers.

sourceAnchors.name: Floyd Lee
sourceAnchors.detail: the sidecar says Floyd Lees dining-in-Iraq example supports meaning, morale, and dignity as emotionally powerful stakes
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Floyd Lees dining room in Iraq points to dignity, not sentimentality, as the emotional engine.

hook: one sad person replaces a statistic every time
make them care as generic command
counterintuition: emotion is not manipulation stated abstractly
identity beats facts as a blanket rule

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person You direct address, retrospective It took her three weeks to see, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.audience: a safety lead addressing machinists who ignore decibel charts
exampleSpecs.stakes: workers risk permanent hearing loss while seeing earplugs as nuisance gear
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Grace plays a recording of one retired machinists muffled grandchild conversation, then ties protection to keeping family voices clear
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The recording sounds like it is playing through a wall

exampleSpecs.audience: a hospital volunteer coordinator writing a campaign for first-time donors
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Hugo replaces regional shortage totals with one surgery slot held open for a named patient status board entry without inventing private details
exampleSpecs.firstImage: At 7:20 a.m., Hugo reads the blank donor column beside Tuesday surgery prep

exampleSpecs.audience: a training director trying to keep first-year apprentices from quitting
exampleSpecs.stakes: the region loses skilled workers if the program feels like hazing
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: "This is not about toughness," Kasia says, then reframes the program as becoming the person trusted near live wires
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "This is not about toughness," Kasia says while the practice panel hums

exampleSpecs.audience: a neighborhood organizer persuading renters and homeowners together
exampleSpecs.stakes: heat risk stays abstract until tied to one bus stop people use
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You watch Sam move from citywide canopy percentages to the noon temperature at the uncovered bus stop where parents wait with strollers
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You can feel the heat coming off the bus shelter bench through your jeans

exampleSpecs.audience: an advisor helping students see why paperwork matters
exampleSpecs.stakes: missed forms can cost a semester, but reminders feel bureaucratic
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Layla connects the form to keeping a students lab coat and campus job, not to compliance language
exampleSpecs.firstImage: It took Layla four unopened reminder emails to see the word deadline was the wrong stake

exampleSpecs.audience: a team lead explaining radio discipline to new volunteers
exampleSpecs.stakes: a casual missed call can delay a real rescue
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Luca frames radio checks as belonging to the kind of team that brings someone home, then shows the empty map square that depends on one clear reply
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Fog presses against the windows of the volunteer hall before dawn

skillTargets: choose the human stake that makes an idea matter
distinguish dignity and identity from manipulation
repair analytical framing that cools care
evaluate when one-person focus stays honest to scale

tryThisNowSpec: Name the person, identity, or dignity stake hidden inside one abstract message, then rewrite the message so that stake appears before the statistic.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
